source: Kim et al. (2025) Limitations of LLMs in clinical problem-solving arising from inflexible reasoning (full PDF re-read)
finding: The only arXiv version served (v1, 5 Feb 2025) names just two best models. DeepSeek-R1 52% and DeepSeek-V3 50% are not in it.
numbers: Gemini-1.5-Pro 50%, o1 48%; most models under 50% on M-ARC; physicians 66%.
quote: most LLMs perform poorly on M-ARC tasks, with less than 50% accuracy
limits: The DeepSeek figures may come from the journal version (PMC12606185, read earlier in a26/b18). No later arXiv version was found.
agent_relevance: Cite 'best 48-52%' and name the source version.

source: Chen et al. (2026) MedEinst Table 1 re-read from PDF text (gap 2)
finding: Table 1 rows re-aligned. Qwen3-32B: base accuracy 44.12, robust accuracy 11.28, bias trap rate 43.46. The ablation start (40.25 base) is a different run of the same model.
limits: Some cells (Claude-Sonnet-4.5, Gemini, Baichuan base accuracy) are still unreadable in text extraction. Alignment was checked by value matching, not by looking at the table image.
agent_relevance: Gap 2 closed for Qwen3-32B: 44.12 base, 43.46 trap.

source: Chen et al. (2026) MedEinst: does higher accuracy mean higher trap rate? (gap 9, own calculation on Table 1)
finding: The paper text says GPT-5 and Gemini-2.5-Pro have the highest base accuracy (54.30, 53.58) and trap rates over 50 percent, so stronger priors mean stronger blindness. The table does not support this: 54.30 and 53.58 sit on the Lingshu-7B and Llama3-Med42-8B rows, and GPT-5 base is 40.51.
numbers: Pearson r between base accuracy and trap rate over the 8 cleanly aligned rows: -0.69 (more accurate models had LOWER trap rate). GPT-5 trap 51.87, Gemini 60.90, Lingshu-7B 36.74. N=8 models, one benchmark.
quote: models that better fit general medical distributions develop stronger priors
limits: Computed by me from garbled table text; small N. Trap rate is conditional on a correct control answer, so models with low control accuracy are scored on fewer cases.
agent_relevance: 'Stronger LLMs are more fixated' is not established by MedEinst. Do not build the schema on it; build on the trap-set mechanism (minimal counterfactual edit).

source: Chen et al. (2026) MedEinst: multi-agent baselines (gap 1)
finding: Generic multi-agent structure did not lower fixation. Debate (MDAgent) and dynamic agent selection (DyLAN), both on Qwen3-32B, scored far worse than the single base model on robust accuracy and gave only small trap-rate changes.
numbers: Robust accuracy: base 11.28, MDAgent 3.20, DyLAN 1.19, ECR-Agent 11.68. Trap rate: base 43.46, MDAgent 40.34, DyLAN 41.69, ECR-Agent 33.75. Ablation: base 40.25 to 55.49 (+DCI) to 69.49 (+memory) base accuracy.
limits: No equal-token run. The authors blame consensus bias. ECR-Agent changes structure AND adds memory and more calls, so the scaffold effect is not isolated.
agent_relevance: Debate-style second routes can amplify the dominant prior. S6 second routes should be forced to differ by evidence, not voted.

source: Shidara et al. (2026) Advances in LLM reasoning enable flexibility in clinical problem-solving (hint/effort check, gap 4)
finding: Models were run at highest reasoning effort with standard CoT. No prompt telling the model about a possible trap was tested.
numbers: Claude 4.1 Opus 0.751; physicians 0.66.
limits: Absence in this paper is not a result. No LLM study of the informed-prompt condition was found (web search budget was exhausted; arXiv search was rate-limited).
agent_relevance: Gap 4 stays open: the informed-prompt test is still ours to run.

source: Wang et al. (2025) Thoughts are all over the place: on the underthinking of o1-like LLMs
finding: A process-level measure exists. Thoughts were split at switch words ('alternatively') with Llama-3.3-70B. Wrong answers contain far more thought switches than right ones. Underthinking score UT = 1 - (tokens up to first correct thought / total tokens), over wrong answers.
numbers: o1-like models used 225% more tokens in incorrect than correct answers, with 418% more thought switches. UT: QwQ-32B-Preview 58.2 (MATH500 L5, acc 84.3), DeepSeek-R1-671B 65.4 (acc 92.5); GPQA Diamond QwQ 48.3, R1 58.8; AIME24 QwQ 65.0, R1-Preview 75.7, R1 37.0.
limits: Math and science QA only, open-weight models. It measures too little depth, the opposite failure to Einstellung (too much commitment). Computing UT needs a check of whether each early thought was correct.
agent_relevance: Gap 3: count route switches and tokens before the first correct route as trace metrics. Fixation needs the reverse: share of tokens on the first route. Neither has been validated against trap accuracy.

source: Wang et al. (2025) Underthinking: thought-switching penalty and a prompt control (gaps 1, 4)
finding: Penalising switch tokens at decoding raised accuracy with no fine-tuning; a prompt saying 'complete every idea, don't give up halfway' gave almost nothing.
numbers: QwQ-32B-Preview Pass@1: AIME24 38.3 to 44.1, GPQA 57.6 to 59.1, MATH500-L5 83.1 to 83.7. R1-Distill-Qwen-32B AIME24 61.4 to 64.1. DeepSeek-R1 AIME24 73.8; +prompt 72.4; +TIP 74.8. Switch tokens (R1) 13.8 to 5.7; interval 580 to 942 tokens. TIP parameters 3 and 600 tuned on AIME22/23.
quote: Although prompt engineering provides certain guidance, Table 3 shows only modest changes
limits: Tuned on a dev set; gains on easier sets are about 0.5 to 1.5 points. Tests persistence, the mirror image of our need to switch.
agent_relevance: A one-line prompt about thought policy changed little; a decoding-level control changed more. Weak support for prompt-only S6 rules.

source: Sui et al. (2026 v6) Meta-Reasoner: dynamic guidance for inference-time reasoning (gap 7)
finding: A contextual-bandit (LinUCB) strategy selector, fed a short progress report, beat letting the LLM pick its own strategy and beat fixed strategy sets.
numbers: Game of 24: GPT-4o-mini CoT 4%, SC-CoT 9%, ToT(b=5) 65%, Reflexion 53%, MACM 80%, Meta-Reasoner 89% (GPT-4o 92%). TheoremQA GPT-4o-mini: CoT 39.46, Meta 84.13. Ablation w/o MAB (direct arm selection) 82 (24) and 79.42 (TheoremQA); w/o progress report 85 and 80.74. Fixed K=3: 65; K=5: 72; dynamic 89 (14 strategies). Time: 51-55% less than o1-preview; 29-33% less than ToT, Reflexion, MACM, Best-of-N.
limits: Not a trap or Einstellung test. Reported by the authors only; the bandit learns from reward over many problems. Monitor cost is given as time and a token figure, not an equal-token table.
agent_relevance: A learned selector beat a fixed menu and self-selection, but the step from self-selection to bandit is 3-7 points on Game of 24 and 4-5 on TheoremQA. Monitor is cheap: one summary per round.

source: Han et al. (2025) HybridMind: meta-selection of natural vs symbolic reasoning (gap 7)
finding: A trained or prompted selector chooses the method per problem. The oracle over methods is far above any single method, so choice matters.
numbers: Fine-tuned Llama-3.1-8B selector beats GPT-4o natural-language reasoning by 4.4% on FOLIO and 1.3% on MATH; prompted GPT-3.5 selector +10% on hard FOLIO subset. Oracle (at least one method right) 10.3% or more above best single method. Selector picks NL 94.10% of the time on MATH and 58.84% on FOLIO.
limits: Two routes only (language vs symbolic). Not about fixation. The selector itself collapses onto the default on MATH.
agent_relevance: Supports operator choice by a separate selector, with the warning that selectors fall back on the default route.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) Reasoning strategies in LLMs: can they follow, prefer and optimize? (gap 7)
finding: Telling the model which logical strategy to use did not change accuracy; the model cannot pick the best strategy without help; an oracle choosing per problem would add a lot.
numbers: TruthQuest (Phi-4 / R1-Distill) and ZebraLogic (Phi-4 / Qwen3). No strategy: 47.2 / 63.4 / 27.3 / 32.0. Four strategy prompts: 45.1-49.0 (Phi-4 TQ), 61.4-63.0 (R1-Distill). Oracle: 82.9 / 90.1 / 37.7 / 36.4. Majority vote over strategies: 54.9 / 68.4 / 27.9 / 32.0. Verifier: 46.9 / 74.1 / 28.2 / 33.4.
limits: Logic puzzles only, 4 prompt strategies; verifier adds decoding cost. Oracle gap is large on TruthQuest and small on ZebraLogic for Qwen3 (32.0 vs 36.4).
agent_relevance: Prompting a strategy does not change accuracy by itself; selection by consensus or a verifier recovers part of the oracle gap.

source: Binz & Schulz (2022/2023) Reconstructing the Einstellung effect: Luchins's thesis data (gap 5)
finding: Luchins's 1942 numbers, retyped from his thesis tables and re-analysed. After 5 set-inducing problems, most students used the long method on test problems where a short one works; control students without training never did.
numbers: Plain group 128/155 (0.83) used the long (E) solution on C1/C2 vs 0/155 controls; C3/C4 100/155 (0.65) vs 0/155; chi2=218.02 and 147.62. N=310.
limits: Reconstruction by the authors, New York college students, 1940s paper test. Not a modern preregistered design.
agent_relevance: Original effect size is large and re-checked. The agent test (a few worked long-method items, then a short-method item) mirrors it.

source: Binz & Schulz (2022/2023): Luchins's manipulations re-analysed (gaps 4, 5)
finding: A warning helped only part way; alternating long and short problems in training helped a lot; time pressure made it worse.
numbers: 'Don't be blind' warning: 87/153 (0.57) vs plain 0.83 on C1/C2 (chi2=24.16). Alternating training: 20/124 (0.16) vs plain 97/121 (0.80). Speedy: 95/98 (0.97) vs plain 126/153 (0.82); on C3/C4 0.99 vs 0.55.
limits: A warning still left 57% fixated; the cost of the warning when the familiar method is right was not tested. The paper also cites Lane & Jensen 1993 and Chrysikou & Weisberg 2005 (defixation instructions cut set effects); those were not opened.
agent_relevance: One-line warning gives a partial effect (about 26 points). Mixed practice beats warnings. Deadlines raise fixation, so a hard token cap may do the same to the agent.

source: Binz & Schulz (2022/2023) resource-rational model of Einstellung (gap 8)
finding: A model that turns prior preferences into a policy under a time cost reproduces plain, control, warning, alternating and speed effects. Time pressure is modelled as a lower inverse temperature. Cheap repetition can be the right trade-off.
numbers: Simulated agents: 90/100 used E on C1/C2 after E-only training vs 23/100 after alternating training (data 0.80 vs 0.16). Plain beta=25, speedy beta=15.
limits: Fits one 1942 dataset; parameters set by hand to match conditions. Gives no direct stop rule for open-ended search.
agent_relevance: Candidate stop rule for S6: keep the first route unless a cheap check shows it is not minimal or the expected gain of another route exceeds its token cost. Needs a test; not validated.

source: Vallee-Tourangeau, Euden & Hearn (2011) Einstellung defused: interactivity and mental set (gap 5)
finding: Independent study of the Luchins water-jar set effect. Using real jars at a sink cut perseverance versus paper problems (two experiments). Visuospatial skill predicted perseverance only in the interactive condition.
numbers: Abstract only: effect 'significantly reduced'; sample sizes and rates not read.
limits: Abstract read through Europe PMC, not full text.
agent_relevance: Acting on the problem (running code, tool calls) may reduce fixation more than re-reading it. Supports an executable check inside S6.

source: Tempel & Frings (2019) Directed forgetting in problem solving (gap 5)
finding: Independent water-jar study: a 'forget the earlier problems' instruction cut use of the practised formula on test problems. In anagrams, the same instruction slowed solving of tests needing the old formula.
numbers: Abstract only: significant reduction in Exp 1; slower test anagrams in Exp 2. No Ns in the abstract.
limits: Abstract-level read. Exp 2 shows an over-switching cost when the old routine is needed.
agent_relevance: A context reset ('forget route A') works but costs when route A is right (gap 4 cost question, in humans).

source: Pope et al. (2015) Baboons, but not humans, break cognitive set in a visuomotor task (gap 5)
finding: Set effect found outside chess and outside verbal tasks: most of 104 humans were hindered by the set, baboons almost unaffected. Children 7-10 broke set better than adolescents and adults.
numbers: 104 humans (ages 7-68) vs 15 baboons; abstract gives no rates.
limits: Abstract-level read. Different task, not expertise.
agent_relevance: Strong learned routines can make a capable system less flexible than a simpler one; not LLM data.

source: Thomas & Didierjean (2016) Magicians fix your mind: how unlikely solutions block obvious ones (gap 5)
finding: One exposure to an unlikely false solution stopped people finding the obvious real secret of a card trick, even when told to look for another.
numbers: Abstract only; no figures read.
limits: Abstract-level read.
agent_relevance: The blocking idea need not be good. A confident wrong first route can block a simple one: rank routes by simplicity too.

source: Sergeyuk et al. (2023) Overcoming the mental set effect in programming problem solving (gap 5)
finding: Programming: 44% of 129 Python developers showed a habitual-inefficient-function mental set, and these had LESS experience (25 vs 37 months). Neither an interface change nor a 'forget previous solutions' instruction helped.
numbers: 57/129 showed the set; experience T(126.998)=2.806, p=.006. Final N=39; only 2 control participants switched to the direct function in the second set. Response-time difference H(2)=1.403, p=.496.
limits: Experience range was months, not expert level; tasks may have been too easy; 39 completers of 57. A null for the interventions, not for the effect.
agent_relevance: Failed intervention transfer: de-automation cues alone did not work in this domain. Experience direction is opposite to chess, so the skill gradient is domain dependent.

source: Bilalic, McLeod & Gobet (2009) Specialization effect in expert chess players (gap 5)
finding: Same lab, different design: knowledge specific to a familiar opening area beat general skill. Players in their own area performed like players 1 SD higher. In own area they searched deeper and narrower; outside it broader and shallower.
numbers: Abstract only; effect about 1 SD of general skill.
limits: Same group as the 2008 study, so not independent.
agent_relevance: Familiarity narrows search breadth. For S6, a familiar problem type should trigger a forced-breadth step.

source: Europe PMC citation list for Bilalic et al. 2008 (PMID 18565505), forward search (gap 5)
finding: 59 citing records. Direct follow-ups on set effects: Sheridan & Reingold 2013 (chess), Ellis & Reingold 2014 (anagrams), Pope-Caldwell 2022, Ninomiya 2022, Vallee-Tourangeau 2011, Tempel & Frings 2019, Thomas & Didierjean 2016, a 2025 neural study of mental-set induction, a 2026 semantic accessibility study. No title is a replication of the GM 100% to CM 0% gradient in chess.
numbers: 59 citing records, checked by title.
limits: Titles only; replications that do not cite it or are not indexed would be missed. Absence is not refutation.
agent_relevance: The skill gradient in absolute terms rests on one lab plus one partial change-of-design replication.

source: Li et al. (2025) LLMs are near-optimal decision-makers with a non-human learning behavior (WCST section, gap 10)
finding: On the Wisconsin Card Sorting Task, most LLMs reached the first set faster and kept set better than humans, but unlike humans they made more perseverative than random errors. DeepSeek matched the human pattern.
numbers: Humans: more non-perseverative than perseverative errors. LLMs except DeepSeek: the reverse. Fig 3 caption: all LLMs outperformed or matched humans.
limits: No link was tested between this score and any trap task. Exact counts not extracted here.
agent_relevance: Gap 10 stays open: the pattern is real but its link to Einstellung accuracy is untested.

source: Mondorf & Plank (2024) as summarised in Zhang et al. (2025): per-model strategy preference
finding: Each LLM leans on one favoured strategy in logical-deduction puzzles; prompts change this only a little (see d10).
numbers: Zhang annotated 100 answers from the no-strategy prompt; percentages sum above 100 because strategies mix.
limits: Second-hand; the original was not opened.
agent_relevance: A default-route bias exists for LLMs on logic tasks, which supports a forced alternative slot.
